title: Upper bound for a curve middle extension
statement:
Let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion of smooth
geometrically connected curves, and let $\mathcal F$ be lisse and
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ on $U_0$. Then

$$
H_c^r(C,j_*\mathcal F)\quad\text{has weights at most }w+r
$$

for every $r$, where $j_*\mathcal F$ is the
middle extension.

proof.text: Choose a dense affine $v:V_0\hookrightarrow U_0$ by [lem-a1-affine-core-of-curve]. Since $U_0$ is a smooth geometrically connected curve, the lemma applies; the complement of $V_0$ in $U_0$ is finite, and the complement of $U_0$ in $C_0$ is finite because it is a closed zero-dimensional subscheme of the finite-type curve $C_0$. The recovery lemma [lem-a1-lisse-middle-extension], applied to the lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $U_0$, identifies $v_* (\mathcal F|_{V_0})$ with $\mathcal F$. Transitivity of ordinary direct image therefore identifies $j_*\mathcal F$ with the middle extension of $\mathcal F|_{V_0}$ along the composite $V_0\hookrightarrow C_0$.

If $\mathcal F$ has rank zero, it is the zero lisse sheaf, so its ordinary direct image and all compactly supported cohomology groups are zero and the conclusion is immediate. Assume henceforth that its rank is at least one. The restriction $\mathcal F|_{V_0}$ remains lisse and punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, so [thm-a1-affine-curve-upper] gives weights at most $w+r$ for $H_c^r(V,\mathcal F)$ and vanishing outside degrees $0,1,2$. For each point of the finite boundary $Z_0=C_0\setminus V_0$, [lem-wf-boundary-semicontinuity] applied to $V_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ gives weights at most $w$ on the stalk of the middle extension; [lem-wf-boundary-stalk-invariants] identifies that stalk with inertia invariants, compatibly with Frobenius. Hence [lem-a1-finite-boundary-weights] gives weights at most $w$ on the degree-zero boundary group, while [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology] says all other boundary cohomology vanishes. The localization triangle [prop-a1-curve-boundary-sequence] yields the long exact sequence. For $r=0$ it has $0\to H_c^0(V,\mathcal F)\to H_c^0(C,j_*\mathcal F)\to B$ with $B$ a subobject of the boundary degree-zero group, so the middle term is an extension of a subobject of $B$ by $H_c^0(V,\mathcal F)$. For $r=1$ it gives a quotient $H_c^1(V,\mathcal F)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(C,j_*\mathcal F)$, and for $r\ge2$ it gives an isomorphism with $H_c^r(V,\mathcal F)$; the same sequence gives vanishing outside $0,1,2$. By [lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds], quotients and subobjects preserve upper weight bounds, and by [lem-a1-extension-bounds], extensions preserve them. Thus the degree-zero group has weights at most $w$, the degree-one group at most $w+1$, and for $r\ge2$ the bound is $w+r$; the boundary bound $w\le w+r$ applies in every nonnegative degree.
